paragraphs.sourceText: The method for making beer has changed over time. Hops (啤酒花)，for example, which give many a modem beer its bitter flavor, are a (26)_______ recent addition to the beverage. This was first mentioned in reference to brewing in the ninth century. Now, researchers have found a (27)_______ingredient in residue (残留物）from 5,000-year-old beer brewing equipment. While digging two pits at a site in the central plains of China, scientists discovered fragments from pots and vessels. The different shapes of the containers (28)_______ they were used to brew, filter, and store beer. They may be ancient “beer-making tools,” and the earliest (29_______ evidence of beer brewing in China, the researchers reported in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. To (30)_______ that theory, the team examined the yellowish, dried (31)_______ inside the vessels. The majority of the grains, about 80%, were from cereal crops like barley (大麦),and about 10% were bits of roots, (32)_______lily, which would have made the beer sweeter, the scientists say. Barley was an unexpected find: the crop was domesticated in Western Eurasia and didn't become a (33)_______food in central China until about 2,000 years ago, according to the researchers. Based on that timing, they indicate barley may have (34)_______
paragraphs.translationZh: 随着时间的推移，酿造啤酒的方法也发生了变化。例如，啤酒花为许多现代啤酒带来了苦味，是最近才添加到饮料中的。这是在九世纪的酿造中首次被提及的。现在，研究人员在具有5000年历史的啤酒酿造设备的残留物中发现了一种令人惊讶的成分。在中国中原的一个地点挖两个坑时，科学家们发现了来自罐子和器皿的碎片。容器的不同形状表明它们被用来酿造、过滤和储存啤酒。它们可能是古代的“啤酒制造工具”，也是中国啤酒酿造的最早的直接证据，研究人员在《科学会刊》上报告说。美国国家科学院的研究小组检查了容器内的黄色干燥残留物，其中大部分（约 80%）来自大麦等谷类作物，约 10% 是一些根茎，其中包括百合，科学家们表示，大麦是一个意外的发现：这种作物在欧亚大陆西部被驯化，直到大约 2000 年前才成为中国中部的主食。研究人员根据这个时间，他们表明大麦可能已经到达了。

paragraphs.sourceText: in the region not as food, but as (35)_______material for beer brewing.

paragraphs.sourceText: The Blessing and Curse of the People Who Never Forget
paragraphs.translationZh: 永不忘记之人的祝福与诅咒

paragraphs.sourceText: A handful of people can recall almost every day of their lives in enormous detail—and after years of research, neuroscientists (神经科学专家) are finally beginning to understand how they do it.
paragraphs.translationZh: 少数人几乎可以回忆起他们生活中的每一天的大量细节——经过多年的研究，神经科学家（神经科学专家）终于开始理解他们是如何做到这一点的。

paragraphs.sourceText: A. For most of us, memory is a mess of blurred and faded pictures of our lives. As much as we would like to cling on to our past, even the saddest moments can be washed away with time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 答：对于我们大多数人来说，记忆是一堆模糊、褪色的生活照片。尽管我们很想牢牢抓住过去，但即使是最悲伤的时刻也会随着时间而消失。

paragraphs.sourceText: B. Ask Nima Veiseh what he was doing for any day in the past 15 years, however, and he will give you the details of the weather, what he was wearing, or even what side of the train he was sitting on his journey to work. “My memory is like a library of video tapes, walk-throughs of every day of my life from waking to sleeping,” he explains.
paragraphs.translationZh: B. 然而，如果问 Nima Veiseh 在过去 15 年中的任何一天他在做什么，他都会告诉你天气的详细信息、他穿的衣服，甚至他在上班途中坐在火车的哪一边。 “我的记忆就像一个录像带库，记录了我从醒来到睡觉的每一天，”他解释道。

paragraphs.sourceText: C. Veiseh can even put a date on when those tapes started recording: 15 December 2000, when he met his first girlfriend at his best friend's 16th birthday party. He had always had a good memory, but the thrill of young love seems to have shifted a gear in his mind: from now on, he would start recording his whole life in detail. “I could tell you everything about every day after that.”
paragraphs.translationZh: C. Veiseh 甚至可以标出这些磁带开始录制的日期：2000 年 12 月 15 日，当时他在他最好的朋友的 16 岁生日聚会上遇到了他的第一个女朋友。他的记忆力一向很好，但年轻时爱情的快感似乎在他的脑海中换了档：从现在开始，他要开始详细记录自己的一生。 “从那以后我可以告诉你每一天的一切。”

paragraphs.sourceText: D. Needless to say, people like Veiseh are of great interest to neuroscientists hoping to understand the way the brain records our lives. A couple of recent papers have finally opened a window on these people’s extraordinary minds. And such research might even suggest ways for us all to relive our past with greater clarity.
paragraphs.translationZh: D. 不用说，神经科学家对像 Veiseh 这样的人非常感兴趣，希望了解大脑记录我们生活的方式。最近的几篇论文终于为我们打开了了解这些人非凡思想的窗口。此类研究甚至可能为我们所有人提供更清晰地重温过去的方法。

paragraphs.sourceText: E. “Highly superior autobiographical memory” （or HSAM for short) first came to light in the early
paragraphs.translationZh: E.“高度优越的自传体记忆”（简称HSAM）早在

paragraphs.sourceText: 2000s, with a young woman named Jill Price. Emailing the neuroscientist and memory researcher Jim McGaugh one day, she claimed that she could recall every day of her life since the age of 12. Could he help explain her experiences?
paragraphs.translationZh: 2000 年代，与一位名叫吉尔·普莱斯 (Jill Price) 的年轻女子在一起。有一天，她给神经科学家兼记忆研究员 Jim McGaugh 发了一封电子邮件，声称自己可以回忆起 12 岁以来的每一天。他能帮助解释一下她的经历吗？

paragraphs.sourceText: F. McGaugh invited her to his lab, and began to test her: he would give her a date and ask her to tell him about the world events on that day. True to her word, she was correct almost every time.
paragraphs.translationZh: F.麦高邀请她到他的实验室，并开始测试她：他会给她一个约会，并要求她告诉他那天发生的世界大事。正如她所说，她几乎每次都是正确的。

paragraphs.sourceText: G. It didn’t take long for magazines and documentary film-makers to come to understand her “total recall”，and thank to the subsequent media interest, a few dozen other subjects (including Veiseh) have since come forward and contacted the team at the University of California, Irvine.
paragraphs.translationZh: G. 没过多久，杂志和纪录片制作人就开始了解她的“全面回忆”，并且由于随后媒体的兴趣，其他几十个受试者（包括 Veiseh）随后站出来联系了加州大学欧文分校的团队。

paragraphs.sourceText: H. Interestingly, their memories are highly self-centred: although they can remember “autobiographical” life events in extraordinary detail, they seem to be no better than average at recalling impersonal information, such as random (任意选取的）lists of words. Nor are they necessarily better at remembering a round of drinks, say. And although their memories are vast, they are still likely to suffer from “false memories”.Clearly, there is no such thing as a “perfect” memory—their extraordinary minds are still using the same flawed tools that the rest of us rely on. The question is, how?
paragraphs.translationZh: H. 有趣的是，他们的记忆是高度以自我为中心的：虽然他们可以非常详细地记住“自传式”生活事件，但他们在回忆非个人信息方面似乎并不比平均水平好，例如随机的（各种各样的）单词列表。他们也不一定更擅长记住一轮饮料，比如说。虽然他们的记忆力很大，但他们仍然可能遭受“错误记忆”的困扰。显然，不存在所谓的“完美”记忆——他们非凡的头脑是不存在的。仍然使用我们其他人所依赖的同样有缺陷的工具，问题是，如何做到这一点？

paragraphs.sourceText: I. Lawrence Patihis at the University of Southern Mississippi recently studied around 20 people with HSAM and found that they scored particularly high on two measures: fantasy proneness (倾向)and absorption. Fantasy proneness could be considered a tendency to imagine and daydream, whereas absorption is the tendency to allow your mind to become fully absorbed in an activity to pay complete attention to the sensations (感受)and the experiences. “I’m extremely sensitive to sounds, smells and visual detail,” explains Nicole Donohue, who has taken part in many of these studies. “I definitely feel things more strongly than the average person.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 南密西西比大学的 I. Lawrence Patihis 最近对大约 20 名 HSAM 患者进行了研究，发现他们在两项指标上得分特别高：倾向性和吸收力。幻想倾向可以被认为是一种想象和白日梦的倾向，而专注是让你的思想完全专注于一项活动以完全关注感觉（感受）和体验的倾向。 “我对声音、气味和视觉细节非常敏感，”参与了许多此类研究的妮可·多诺霍 (Nicole Donohue) 解释道。 “我对事物的感受肯定比一般人更强烈。”

paragraphs.sourceText: J. The absorption helps them to establish strong foundations for recollection, says Patihis, and the fantasy proneness means that they revisit those memories again and again in the coming weeks and months. Each time this initial memory trace is “replayed”, it becomes even stronger. In some ways, you probably go through that process after a big event like your wedding day,but the difference is that thanks to their other psychological tendencies, the HSAM subjects are doing it day in, day out, for the whole of their lives.
paragraphs.translationZh: J. 帕蒂希斯说，全神贯注有助于他们为回忆打下坚实的基础，而幻想倾向意味着他们会在接下来的几周和几个月内一次又一次地重温这些记忆。每一次“重放”这个最初的记忆痕迹，它都会变得更加强烈。在某些方面，你可能会在婚礼等重大事件之后经历这个过程，但不同的是，由于他们的其他心理倾向，HSAM 对象在他们的一生中日复一日地这样做。

paragraphs.sourceText: K. Not everyone with a tendency to fantasise will develop HSAM, though, so Patihis suggests that something must have caused them to think so much about their past. “Maybe some experience in their childhood meant that they became obsessed (着迷）with calendars and what happened to them,” says Patihis. 第7 页共12 页
paragraphs.translationZh: K. 不过，并不是每个有幻想倾向的人都会发展出 HSAM，因此帕蒂希斯认为一定有什么原因导致他们对自己的过去思考得如此之多。 “也许他们童年的一些经历意味着他们对日历和发生在他们身上的事情着迷，”帕蒂希斯说。

paragraphs.sourceText: L. The people with HSAM I’ve interviewed would certainly agree that it can be a mixed blessing. On the plus side, it allows you to relive the most transformative and enriching experiences. Veiseh, for instance, travelled a lot in his youth. In his spare time, he visited the local art galleries, and the paintings are now lodged deep in his autobiographical memories.
paragraphs.translationZh: L. 我采访过的拥有 HSAM 的人肯定会同意，这可能是一件好事。从好的方面来说，它可以让您重温最具变革性和丰富性的经历。例如，维塞年轻时就经常旅行。闲暇时，他参观了当地的美术馆，这些画作如今已深深烙印在他的自传记忆中。

paragraphs.sourceText: M. “Imagine being able to remember every painting, on every wall, in every gallery space, between nearly 40 countries ，” he says. “That’s a big education in art by itself.” With this comprehensive knowledge of the history of art, he has since become a professional painter.
paragraphs.translationZh: M. “想象一下，能够记住近 40 个国家/地区的每面墙上、每个画廊空间中的每一幅画，”他说。 “这本身就是一次伟大的艺术教育。”凭借对艺术史的全面了解，他从此成为一名职业画家。

paragraphs.sourceText: N. Donohue, now a history teacher, agrees that it helped during certain parts of her education. “I can definitely remember what I learned on certain days at school. I could imagine what the teacher was saying or what it looked like in the book.”
paragraphs.translationZh: N. Donohue 现在是一名历史老师，她也同意这对她的某些教育阶段有所帮助。 “我绝对记得在学校的某些日子里学到了什么。我可以想象老师在说什么或者书上的内容。”

paragraphs.sourceText: O. Not everyone with HSAM has experienced these benefits, however. Viewing the past in high definition can make it very difficult to get over pain and regret. “It can be very hard to forget embarrassing moments,” says Donohue. “You feel the same emotions—it is just as raw, just as fresh... You can’t turn off that stream of memories, no matter how hard you try.” Veiseh agrees. “It is like having these open wounds—they are just a part of you,” he says. [P] This means they often have to make a special effort to lay the past to rest. Bill, for instance, often gets painful “flashbacks”，in which unwanted memories intrude into his consciousness, but overall he has chosen to see it as the best way of avoiding repeating the same mistakes. “Some people are absorbed in the past but not open to new memories, but that’s not the case for me. I look forward to each day and experiencing something new.”
paragraphs.translationZh: O. 然而，并不是每个拥有 HSAM 的人都体验到了这些好处。以高清的方式回顾过去可能会让人很难克服痛苦和遗憾。 “很难忘记尴尬的时刻，”多诺霍说。 “你会感受到同样的情绪——同样原始、同样新鲜……无论你如何努力，你都无法关闭那段记忆流。”维塞表示同意。 “就像这些开放性伤口一样——它们只是你的一部分，”他说。 [P] 这意味着他们常常必须付出特别的努力来安息过去。例如，比尔经常会经历痛苦的“闪回”，其中不想要的记忆侵入他的意识，但总的来说，他选择将其视为避免重复同样错误的最佳方式。 “有些人沉迷于过去，却不愿接受新的记忆，但对我来说不是这样。我期待着每一天，体验新的事物。”

paragraphs.sourceText: 36.People with HSAM have the same memory as ordinary people when it comes to impersonal information.
paragraphs.translationZh: 36.具有HSAM的人对于非个人信息的记忆力与普通人相同。

paragraphs.sourceText: 37.Fantasy proneness will not necessarily cause people to develop HSAM.
paragraphs.translationZh: 37.幻想倾向并不一定会导致人们发展HSAM。

paragraphs.sourceText: 38.Veiseh began to remember the details of his everyday experiences after he met his first young love.
paragraphs.translationZh: 38.维塞在遇到他的初恋情人后开始回忆起他每天经历的细节。

paragraphs.sourceText: 39.Many more people with HSAM started to contact researchers due to the mass media.
paragraphs.translationZh: 39.由于大众媒体，更多患有 HSAM 的人开始联系研究人员。

paragraphs.sourceText: 40.People with HSAM often have to make efforts to avoid focusing on the past.
paragraphs.translationZh: 40.患有HSAM的人常常必须努力避免关注过去。

paragraphs.sourceText: 41.Most people do not have clear memories of past events.
paragraphs.translationZh: 41.大多数人对过去的事件没有清晰的记忆。

paragraphs.sourceText: 42.HSAM can be both a curse and a blessing.
paragraphs.translationZh: 42.HSAM既可以是诅咒，也可以是祝福。

paragraphs.sourceText: 43.A young woman sought explanation from a brain scientist when she noticed her unusual memory.
paragraphs.translationZh: 43.一名年轻女子发现自己异常的记忆力后，向脑科学家寻求解释。

paragraphs.sourceText: 44.Some people with HSAM find it very hard to get rid of unpleasant memories.
paragraphs.translationZh: 44.一些患有 HSAM 的人发现很难摆脱不愉快的记忆。

paragraphs.sourceText: 45.A recent study of people with HSAM reveals that they are liable to fantasy and full absorption in an activity.
paragraphs.translationZh: 45. 最近对 HSAM 患者的一项研究表明，他们容易产生幻想并全神贯注于某项活动。

For each of them there are four choices marked A), B), C) and D). You should decide on the best choice and mark the corresponding letter on Answer Sheet 2with a single line through the centre.
paragraphs.translationZh: 说明：本节有 2 段。每段文章后面都有一些问题或未完成的陈述。每个选项都有四个选项，标记为 A)、B)、C) 和 D)。您应该决定最佳选择，并在答题纸 2 上用一条穿过中心的单线标记相应的字母。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 46 至 50 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: The phrase almost completes itself: midlife crisis. It’s the stage in the middle of the journey when people feel youth vanishing, their prospects narrowing and death approaching.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这句话几乎已经完成了：中年危机。这是人生旅途中的一个阶段，人们感到青春消逝、前途渺茫、死亡临近。

paragraphs.sourceText: There’s only one problem with the cliche (套话).It isn’t true.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这套话只有一个问题。这不是真的。

paragraphs.sourceText: “In fact, there is almost no hard evidence for midlife crisis other than a few small pilot studies conducted decades ago,” Barbara Hagerty writes in her new book, Life Reimagined. The vast bulk of the research shows that there may be a pause, or a shifting of gears in the 40s or 50s, but this shift “can be exciting, rather than terrifying”.
paragraphs.translationZh: “事实上，除了几十年前进行的一些小型试点研究之外，几乎没有任何确凿的证据表明中年危机，”芭芭拉·哈格蒂在她的新书《重新想象的生活》中写道。大量研究表明，40 年代或 50 年代可能会出现停顿或转变，但这种转变“可能令人兴奋，而不是令人恐惧”。

paragraphs.sourceText: Barbara Hagerty looks at some of the features of people who turn midlife into a rebirth. They break routines, because “autopilot is death”. They choose purpose over happiness 一having a clear sense of purpose even reduces the risk of Alzheimer’s disease. They give priority to relationships, as careers often recede(逐渐淡化).
paragraphs.translationZh: 芭芭拉·哈格蒂（Barbara Hagerty）着眼于那些将中年转为重生的人的一些特征。他们打破常规，因为“自动驾驶就是死亡”。他们选择目标而不是幸福——拥有明确的目标甚至可以降低患阿尔茨海默病的风险。他们优先考虑人际关系，因为事业往往会退步（逐渐淡化）。

paragraphs.sourceText: Life Reimagined paints a picture of middle age that is far from gloomy. Midlife seems like the second big phase of decision-making. Your identity has been formed; you’ve built up your resources; and now you have the chance to take the big risks precisely because your foundation is already secure.
paragraphs.translationZh: 《重新想象的生活》描绘了一幅远非悲观的中年图景。中年似乎是决策的第二个重要阶段。你的身份已经形成；你已经积累了你的资源；现在你有机会冒很大的风险，因为你的基础已经稳固了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Karl Barth described midlife precisely this way. At middle age, he wrote, “the sowing is behind; now is the time to reap. The run has been taken; now is the time to leap. Preparation has been made; now is the time for the venture of the work itself.”
paragraphs.translationZh: 卡尔·巴特正是这样描述中年的。到了中年，他写道：“播种已经过去了，现在是收获的时候了。奔跑已经开始了，现在是跳跃的时候了。准备工作已经做好了，现在是冒险工作本身的时候了。”

paragraphs.sourceText: The middle-aged person, Barth continued, can see death in the distance, but moves with a “measured haste” to get big new things done while there is still time.
paragraphs.translationZh: 巴特继续说，中年人可以看到远处的死亡，但会“谨慎地仓促”行动，趁还有时间完成重大的新事情。

paragraphs.sourceText: What Barth wrote decades ago is even truer today. People are healthy and energetic longer. We have presidential candidates running for their first term in office at age 68, 69 and 74. A longer lifespan is
paragraphs.translationZh: 巴特几十年前所写的内容在今天更加正确。人们健康、精力充沛的时间更长。我们有 68 岁、69 岁和 74 岁的总统候选人参加他们的第一个任期。更长的寿命是

paragraphs.sourceText: changing the narrative structure of life itself. What could have been considered the beginning of a descent is now a potential turning point—the turning point you are most equipped to take full advantage of.
paragraphs.translationZh: 改变生活本身的叙事结构。本来可以被认为是下降的开始现在却是一个潜在的转折点——你最有能力充分利用的转折点。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 问题 51 至 55 基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: In spring, chickens start laying again, bringing a welcome source of protein at winter’s end. So it’s no surprise that cultures around the world celebrate spring by honoring the egg.
paragraphs.translationZh: 春天，鸡再次开始产蛋，为冬末带来了受欢迎的蛋白质来源。因此，世界各地的文化通过尊重鸡蛋来庆祝春天也就不足为奇了。

paragraphs.sourceText: Some traditions are simple, like the red eggs that get baked into Greek Easter breads. Others elevate the egg into a fancy art, like the heavily jewel-covered “eggs” that were favored by the Russians starting in the 19th century. 第10 页共12 页
paragraphs.translationZh: 有些传统很简单，比如将红鸡蛋烤成希腊复活节面包。另一些人则将鸡蛋提升为一种奇特的艺术，就像从 19 世纪开始深受俄罗斯人喜爱的镶满珠宝的“鸡蛋”。

paragraphs.sourceText: One ancient form of egg art comes to us from Ukraine. For centuries, Ukrainians have been drawing complicated patterns on eggs. Contemporary artists have followed this tradition to create eggs that speak to the anxieties of our age: Life is precious, and delicate. Eggs are, too.
paragraphs.translationZh: 一种古老的鸡蛋艺术形式来自乌克兰。几个世纪以来，乌克兰人一直在鸡蛋上绘制复杂的图案。当代艺术家遵循这一传统，创作出表达我们这个时代焦虑的鸡蛋：生命是宝贵的，也是脆弱的。鸡蛋也是。

paragraphs.sourceText: “There’s something about their delicate nature that appeals to me,” says New Yorker cartoonist Roz Chast. Several years ago, she became interested in eggs and learned the traditional Ukrainian technique to draw her very modem characters. “I’ve broken eggs at every stage of the process—from the very beginning to the very, very end.”
paragraphs.translationZh: “它们微妙的天性吸引了我，”《纽约客》漫画家罗兹·查斯特说。几年前，她对鸡蛋产生了兴趣，并学习了乌克兰传统技术来绘制非常现代的人物。 “我在这个过程的每个阶段都打破了鸡蛋——从一开始到最后。”

paragraphs.sourceText: But there’s an appeal in that vulnerability. “There’s part of this sickening horror of knowing you’re walking on the edge with this, that I kind of like, knowing that it could all fall apart at any second.” Chast’s designs, such as a worried man alone in a tiny rowboat, reflect that delicateness.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但这个漏洞有一个吸引力。 “知道自己正走在边缘，这种令人作呕的恐惧有一部分，我有点喜欢，因为知道这一切都可能随时崩溃。”查斯特的设计，比如一个忧心忡忡的男人独自坐在一艘小划艇上，就体现了这种精致。

paragraphs.sourceText: Traditional Ukrainian decorated eggs also spoke to those fears. The elaborate patterns were believed to offer protection against evil.
paragraphs.translationZh: 传统的乌克兰装饰鸡蛋也表达了这些恐惧。人们相信这些精致的图案可以抵御邪恶。

paragraphs.sourceText: “There’s an ancient legend that as long as these eggs are made, evil will not prevail in the world,” says Joan Brander, a Canadian egg-painter who has been painting eggs for over 60 years, having learned the art from her Ukrainian relatives.
paragraphs.translationZh: “有一个古老的传说，只要这些鸡蛋被制作出来，邪恶就不会在世界上盛行，”加拿大鸡蛋画家琼·布兰德 (Joan Brander) 说，她从乌克兰亲戚那里学到了绘画鸡蛋的艺术，已有 60 多年的历史。

paragraphs.sourceText: The tradition, dating back to 300 B.C., was later incorporated into the Christian church. The old symbols, however, still endure. A decorated egg with a bird on it, given to a young married couple, is a wish for children. A decorated egg thrown into the field would be a wish for a good harvest.
paragraphs.translationZh: 这一传统可以追溯到公元前 300 年，后来被纳入基督教会。然而，旧的符号仍然存在。送给一对年轻夫妇的装饰有小鸟的鸡蛋，是对孩子的愿望。将装饰好的鸡蛋扔进田里，寓意着丰收。
